statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete. Category and cart path failures are findings rather than audit blockers because the homepage and sign-in remained inspectable.

page.notes: Public US retail commerce site. Representative category and cart routes returned the site error state. paths.description: Homepage, representing global shell, discovery, promotions, search entry, responsiveness and loading behavior.
Appliances category listing, representing product discovery. Navigation returned the site error page, so deeper listing inspection was unavailable.
Sign-in flow, representing account forms and modern authentication.
Cart, representing the primary commercial journey and recovery state. It returned the site error page.

findings.summary: The storefront ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The preferences screenshot remains a bright white/light interface, the computed color-scheme is normal, and CSS inspection found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, control and image treatments.

findings.summary: No explicit increased-contrast or forced-colors adaptation was found.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules; Lighthouse separately found four insufficient-contrast groups.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations and test essential controls in Windows High Contrast Mode.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found no view-transition usage, while the site exposes many route and overlay state changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document and cross-document View Transitions for major route and state continuity, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Sign-in and chat prompts compete with shopping content on load.
findings.evidence: Under the combined preferences condition, a sign-in sheet covers the bottom of the mobile viewport while a vertical Live Chat control overlays the content edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay nonessential prompts until user intent is clear, and keep them compact, dismissible and non-overlapping.

findings.summary: The loaded overlay UI does not use native dialog or popover primitives.
findings.evidence: The homepage displayed sign-in and chat overlays, but the DOM probe found 0 dialog elements and 0 popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement modal flows with dialog and transient anchored UI with popover, including declarative light dismiss and focus management.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch target support are incomplete.
findings.evidence: A focused search input computed to transparent outline and zero box-shadow; the UI probe counted 15 rendered controls below 24px in one dimension and Lighthouse failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a clearly visible :focus-visible indicator and enlarge or space interactive targets to WCAG target guidance.

findings.summary: Core product discovery and cart routes failed.
findings.evidence: Direct navigation to the Appliances category and Cart both rendered “Oops!! Something went wrong. Please refresh page” instead of products or cart content.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix shell/API initialization for category and cart routes, then add automated journey coverage from search/category through cart and checkout.

findings.summary: The core-route error state offers only a blind refresh.
findings.evidence: The category and cart error screens provide a Refresh button but no cause, preserved context, alternate route, retry status, or useful recovery steps.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve context and provide actionable retry, back, support and fallback navigation with accessible status announcements.

findings.summary: Lab loading performance is well outside good Core Web Vitals ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.9s, FCP 4.9s, TBT 2,180ms and performance 28; the CDP trace measured LCP 5.56s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image/content, reduce critical scripting, and verify field and lab LCP/INP/CLS after changes.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded 10 long tasks, a 252.82ms longest task and 589.24ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 2,180ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile long tasks, split work, defer analytics/personalization and schedule noncritical tasks by priority.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is too heavy for the landing experience.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 138 requests and 3.96MB transferred, including 2.79MB of script and multiple parser-inserted high-priority resources; Lighthouse total byte weight was 5,529KiB.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten critical dependency chains, defer noncritical scripts and styles, and make the LCP asset immediately discoverable and prioritized.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial avoidable JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 1,799KiB of unused JavaScript; the HAR recorded 69 script requests totaling 2.79MB, including an 816KB homepage metadata bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused/duplicate modules, route-split bundles, and load personalization and analytics only when needed.

findings.summary: Some form controls lack programmatic labels or matching accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed form labels and label-content-name matching; the DOM probe found homepage search and email inputs with zero associated label elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control an associated label or accurate accessible name and ensure visible and accessible names match.

findings.summary: Text and controls include insufficient color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed four element groups on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in every interactive and promotional state.

findings.summary: The homepage lacks a coherent semantic structure and visible search focus.
findings.evidence: There is no h1, no main or navigation landmark, headings begin at h3 and jump to h5, and the focused search control has a transparent outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1, main/nav landmarks, sequential headings and visible focus indicators with logical tab order.

findings.summary: Touch target sizing does not consistently support reflowed/mobile use.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed target-size and the UI probe found 15 rendered controls smaller than 24px in at least one dimension, although 360px layout did not overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target hit areas and spacing while retaining the current overflow-free mobile reflow.

findings.summary: The homepage logs runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured CORS failure, repeated Apollo invariant exceptions, geolocation failure and store initialization TypeErrors.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve API/CORS and state initialization failures and prevent expected failures from surfacing as uncaught exceptions.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery are not consistently sound.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 15 images without dimensions, 33 without srcset, 18 legacy-format assets and 5 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit valid intrinsic dimensions, responsive sources and modern formats for content images.

findings.summary: The page triggers platform hygiene failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three deprecated API warnings, missing source maps, DevTools Issues, third-party cookies and a geolocation request on page load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated/unload usage, publish source maps, resolve DevTools issues and request location only after an explicit user action.

findings.summary: Core homepage content is absent from raw server HTML.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 1% raw/rendered word coverage and classified the page as a JavaScript shell; raw HTML lacked title, h1 and meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render or statically render meaningful homepage content and metadata so non-JS crawlers receive the real page.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but baseline security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no CSP, HSTS or X-Content-Type-Options; the cookie probe found 41 flagged cookies, including many without Secure and many SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff and secure cookie attributes appropriate to each cookie.

findings.summary: The homepage has a very large tracking and third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe contacted 54 third-party origins and identified 10 known tracker domains; the HAR attributes 118 requests and 3.12MB to non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and remove low-value trackers, gate optional vendors behind consent, and batch/minimize analytics payloads.

findings.summary: Geolocation is requested before an explicit user action.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse geolocation-on-start identified two calls from localizerAutoInit; this also produced a console geolocation error. Sign-in does support autocomplete="username webauthn".
findings.suggestedFix: Move geolocation behind a clearly explained store-location action while retaining WebAuthn-capable sign-in.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: No X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, or CSP was observed on the main response.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and HSTS, and evaluate Trusted Types for the large client app.

findings.summary: Core content depends almost entirely on JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML contained only 3 content tokens versus 125 rendered tokens, with 1% coverage and no raw title or description.
findings.suggestedFix: Deliver core navigation, promotional text and product-discovery entry points in server HTML, then enhance client-side.

findings.summary: Distinct core routes fail during runtime initialization.
findings.evidence: Appliances listing and cart both rendered the generic site error page; Lighthouse captured store initialization TypeErrors and Apollo invariant exceptions.
findings.suggestedFix: Make route data dependencies conditional and sequenced, provide cached/fallback content, and test direct navigation across templates.

findings.summary: Failure states do not provide robust recovery.
findings.evidence: Category and cart failures collapse to a generic full-page error with only Refresh and no preserved task state or alternate path.
findings.suggestedFix: Add bounded retries, offline/network-specific messages, preserved cart/query state and alternative navigation.

findings.summary: The cart journey is not reliably available.
findings.evidence: Direct navigation to Cart returned a full-page error instead of cart contents or a safe continuation path; sign-in loaded successfully but purchase continuity could not proceed.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore cart reliability, preserve cart state through failures and verify clear pricing/commitments through checkout.

findings.summary: Promotional imagery is frequently oversized or delivered in legacy formats.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 5 oversized assets, 18 legacy-format assets, 33 images without responsive sources and 9 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Use AVIF/WebP, responsive srcset/sizes, correct intrinsic dimensions and lazy loading for below-fold promotions.

findings.summary: Background personalization, analytics and tracking create disproportionate work.
findings.evidence: The homepage made 138 requests, 69 for scripts, while Lighthouse estimated 1,799KiB unused JavaScript and the trace recorded 10 long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer, conditionally load or remove nonessential analytics, personalization and survey work, especially before interaction.

findings.summary: Third-party resource use exceeds a proportionate homepage budget.
findings.evidence: 118 of 138 HAR requests and 3.12MB of 3.96MB transferred were non-main-origin; the tracker probe saw 54 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party request/byte budget, remove redundant vendors and load optional integrations only on user demand.

findings.summary: Heap growth after repeated search interaction warrants leak investigation.
findings.evidence: After ten focus/input/clear/blur cycles, the heap summary rose from 1,413,367 to 1,837,904 nodes and from 86.0MB to 107.6MB self size; separate cold sessions lower confidence but the 25% growth is material.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat in one instrumented session with forced GC and baseline/target/final snapshots, then remove retained listeners, buffers or caches identified by dominator paths.

findings.summary: The initial homepage JavaScript heap is large for a promotional landing page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap contained 1.41 million nodes, 6.38 million edges and 86.0MB self size; the post-interaction snapshot reached 107.6MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce loaded bundles and vendor runtimes, release transient data and set a heap/DOM budget for the homepage.
